headline: Microsoft attributed a record 570-flaw Patch Tuesday—two zero-days already under attack—to AI-assisted bug discovery, as SAP, Adobe, VMware, SonicWall, and Progress piled critical fixes onto the same day.

emerging_trends.text: Microsoft blamed artificial intelligence for a record 570-flaw Patch Tuesday, the clearest sign yet that AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is inflating patch volumes faster than defenders can absorb them.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Microsoft Ships a Record 570-Flaw Patch Tuesday

emerging_trends.text: Attackers hit internet-facing appliances from SonicWall and Progress with fresh zero-days, forcing emergency reimaging and password resets while patches lagged the exploitation.
emerging_trends.topic_title: SonicWall and ShareFile Zero-Days Under Active Attack

emerging_trends.text: AI coding and browser assistants keep leaking their users' data, with Cursor auto-running malicious repo code, Claude for Chrome exposing Gmail to rogue extensions, and Grok Build uploading whole Git histories to xAI storage.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Assistants Leak User Data and Run Untrusted Code

topics.title: Microsoft Ships a Record 570-Flaw Patch Tuesday
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft fixed 570 vulnerabilities on July 14, 2026—nearly triple June's record and 622 counting Chromium fixes in Edge—crediting AI-assisted discovery, and warned that two zero-days in Active Directory and SharePoint Server are already exploited while a BitLocker bug went public before the patch.
topics.summary: The July release patches 62 critical flaws and the actively attacked SharePoint remote-code-execution bugs CVE-2026-32201, CVE-2026-45659, and CVE-2026-56164, which CISA separately urged on-premises SharePoint Server 2016, 2019, and Subscription Edition operators to harden. Administrators should apply the Windows and SharePoint updates immediately.

sources.title: Microsoft Patches a Record 570 Security Flaws
Microsoft July 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes massive 570 flaws, 3 zero-days
Microsoft Patches Record 622 Vulnerabilities, Including Two Exploited Zero-Days
CISA Urges SharePoint Hardening After New Exploitations

topics.title: SAP, Adobe, and VMware Rush Critical Enterprise Patches
topics.latest_developments: On July 14, 2026 SAP fixed 16 flaws including the CVSS 9.9 NetWeaver Application Server ABAP out-of-bounds write CVE-2026-44747 plus critical Commerce Cloud and AppRouter bugs, Adobe patched critical ColdFusion code-execution and privilege-escalation defects, and VMware repaired seven severe Avi Load Balancer vulnerabilities.
topics.summary: The flaws span authentication bypass, remote code execution, privilege escalation, and directory traversal across widely deployed business software. Enterprises running SAP NetWeaver, ColdFusion, or VMware Avi should prioritize these fixes alongside the Microsoft rollout.

sources.title: SAP Patches CVSS 9.9 NetWeaver ABAP Flaw That Could Expose or Modify Data
Adobe Patches Critical ColdFusion Vulnerabilities

SAP warns of critical flaws in NetWeaver and Commerce Cloud

topics.title: AI Assistants Leak User Data and Run Untrusted Code
topics.latest_developments: Researchers reported on July 14, 2026 that a ClaudeBleed-linked flaw survives eight patches and lets any extension running on claude.ai trigger Claude for Chrome to read a victim's Gmail, Google Docs, and Calendar, that Cursor still auto-executes malicious code from poisoned repositories despite a December report, and that xAI's Grok Build CLI uploaded entire Git repositories, full commit history included, to a Google Cloud Storage bucket.
topics.summary: Agentic AI coding and browsing tools expose data through over-broad permissions and unsafe defaults. Anthropic, Cursor, and xAI users should restrict which extensions load, avoid opening untrusted repositories in AI IDEs, and audit what these agents transmit.

sources.title: Researchers Say Claude for Chrome Flaw Lets Rogue Extensions Trigger Gmail Reads
Unpatched Claude for Chrome Flaw Lets Extensions Read Gmail, Calendar
Cursor IDE Auto-Executes Malicious Code in Poisoned Repos
Grok Build Uploaded Entire Git Repositories to xAI Storage, Not Just Files It Read

topics.title: Fake GitHub Repos, RATs, and Phishing Kits Spread Infostealers
topics.latest_developments: On July 14, 2026 researchers found a threat actor running nearly 300 GitHub repositories that impersonate legitimate software and security projects to push infostealers, Blackpoint Cyber documented the new Rust-based LabubaRAT masquerading as NVIDIA software to seize Windows hosts, and two phishing kits, Jalisco and OmegaLord, surfaced defeating multi-factor authentication on Microsoft 365 accounts.
topics.summary: The campaigns lean on trust in familiar brands, from GitHub projects and NVIDIA drivers to LastPass and Bitwarden security alerts, to harvest credentials and deploy malware. Users should download software only from verified sources, distrust unsolicited password-manager warnings, and pair MFA with phishing-resistant authentication.

sources.title: Nearly 300 GitHub repos pose as legit software to push malware

topics.title: SonicWall and ShareFile Zero-Days Under Active Attack
topics.latest_developments: SonicWall patched two exploited flaws, CVE-2026-15409 and CVE-2026-15410, in its Secure Mobile Access 1000 Series appliances on July 14, 2026, while Progress Software confirmed a high-severity zero-day drove last week's emergency shutdown of ShareFile Storage Zone Controllers and released a fix.
topics.summary: Both vendors sell internet-facing remote-access gear that attackers reach directly. SonicWall tells organizations showing its indicators of compromise to reimage hardware or redeploy virtual appliances and reset all user and administrator passwords; ShareFile customers should apply the new patch and rebuild affected Windows servers.

sources.title: SonicWall SMA appliances targeted in zero-day attacks (CVE-2026-15409, CVE-2026-15410)
Progress confirms ShareFile zero-day flaw behind Storage Zone shutdown

topics.title: Old Signed Shims Reopen the UEFI Secure Boot Bypass
topics.latest_developments: ESET researchers disclosed on July 14, 2026 that 11 old Microsoft-signed Linux UEFI shims, all version 0.9 or below, let attackers run untrusted code during boot and plant bootkits on most Secure Boot systems; Microsoft revoked them in its June update.
topics.summary: A shim is a small first-stage loader Microsoft signs so Linux and boot tools launch under Secure Boot. Because nearly every UEFI machine trusts that certificate, the vulnerable shims undo the protection; the number of systems still carrying them is unknown, so administrators should apply the revocation and firmware updates.

sources.title: 11 Old Microsoft-Signed Linux UEFI Shims Could Let Attackers Bypass Secure Boot
No one knows how many old shims can still bypass UEFI Secure Boot

around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT will explosively demolish the Interstate 376 Commercial Street Bridge on Wednesday, July 15, between 1 p.m. and 9 p.m., weather permitting.
